name: Review a client's investment policy and asset mix
summary: Each client owns its statement of investment policies and procedures and its strategic asset mix, and its board must review and confirm or amend the policy at least once a year. The asset manager's portfolio construction team does the analysis: every few years a full asset-liability study with the client's actuary and board workshops, and in other years a lighter annual review against new capital market assumptions and the latest valuation. Recommendations pass internal review by the head of portfolio construction and the CIO, then the client's staff, investment committee and board, before the approved targets, ranges, benchmarks and restrictions are keyed into the rebalancing, risk, compliance and performance systems. Most elapsed time is spent waiting for the actuary's projections and for committee and board meeting dates, and board requests for more scenarios add whole rounds.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about 240 staff that invests about $79 billion for a few public pension plans and an insurance board through pooled funds and segregated accounts, on a cost recovery basis.
baseline.notes: Five client portfolios in 2021. The client's board decides; the asset manager advises and implements. Capital market assumptions and risk reports come from other processes. Implementation of a new mix over several years runs through rebalancing.

unit_of_work: one client portfolio's policy and asset mix review
trigger: The client's annual policy review falls due on its governance calendar, or a full asset-liability study is due (every three to five years) or brought forward by a change in funding, plan design or capital market assumptions.
end_state: The client's board has approved or confirmed its policy and asset mix, and any changes are loaded and cross-checked in the rebalancing, risk, compliance and performance systems, with the client told when they take effect.

volume.seasonality: Bunched before year-end board meetings (The pension client approved its SIP&P in December in 2024 and 2025; the insurance client in December 2025); full studies run over most of a year.

evidence.note: Five portfolios each reviewed at least annually plus occasional extra reviews, about 5.4 a year as in the organisation file; one in four is a full study.

steps.name: Open the review and agree scope with the client
steps.description: The relationship manager checks the client's governance calendar, confirms with the client's staff whether this year is a routine annual review of the policy or a full asset-liability study (due every three to five years, or earlier after a large change in funded status or plan design), and books the investment committee and board dates the work must meet.

error.defect_description: Wrong board date or scope assumed, forcing a rushed schedule later.

evidence.note: A/L study every three to five years (The pension client) or at least every four years (The insurance client) with annual policy review; with five portfolios about one in four reviews is a full study. Touch and wait are author estimates.

steps.name: Request liability projections from the client's actuary
steps.description: The portfolio strategist sends the client's actuary a data request: projected benefit cash flows, liability duration and inflation sensitivity, contribution policy, the latest valuation assumptions and any plan changes, in a format the asset-liability model can load.

error.defect_description: Request misses a cash flow breakdown the model needs.

evidence.note: The model manager works with client actuaries on liability characteristics; the pension client's study used its actuaries. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Client actuary delivers liability projections
steps.description: The client's actuary runs the projections from its valuation system and sends cash flow files and a covering note. The work is fitted around the actuary's valuation and funding work for the client.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate of an actuarial consultant's turnaround for a projection outside the valuation cycle.

steps.name: Validate the liability data
steps.description: A portfolio construction analyst loads the cash flows, checks totals against the last valuation, duration and inflation linkage against the actuary's note, and flags gaps or inconsistencies back to the actuary.

error.defect_description: A mismatch between projection and valuation passes unnoticed.

evidence.note: Author estimate; 15% query rate assumed.

steps.name: Run asset-liability projections of candidate mixes
steps.description: The analyst loads the house capital market assumptions, the client's current mix and the liabilities into the asset-liability model and projects assets, liabilities, funded status and contributions over 10 to 30 years under thousands of scenarios for the current mix and several candidate mixes, plus deterministic stress cases such as an inflation shock or equity crash.

error.defect_description: A modelling error (wrong correlation, currency or rebalancing assumption) skews results.

evidence.note: Study projects assets and liabilities under many scenarios and models candidate portfolios; the model manager stress tests include higher inflation. Hours are author estimates.

steps.name: Design and compare candidate asset mixes
steps.description: The portfolio strategist reviews the projections, shapes candidate mixes that respect the client's liquidity needs, private market pacing and leverage limits, compares expected return, funded status risk and contribution risk, and selects two or three options to show the client's board.

error.defect_description: An option ignores a liquidity or pacing constraint.

evidence.note: Liquidity to avoid forced selling and private asset pacing shape the options. Hours are author estimates.

steps.name: Independent risk review of the study
steps.description: A senior risk manager reviews the stress tests, liquidity coverage and leverage of each shortlisted mix with the risk system, checks the model assumptions against the house view and writes a short independent opinion, or sends the work back for corrections.

error.defect_description: A risk in an option is understated.

control.basis: The model manager second-line risk review of asset mix advice before it goes to a client board (common practice at Canadian public pension managers)

evidence.note: The model manager's investment risk division reviews new investments independently (organisation file); its role in asset mix advice and the 15% return rate are author estimates.

steps.name: Run an education workshop with the client's board
steps.description: The portfolio strategist, with the relationship manager, takes the client's board or investment committee through the study: liabilities, capital market assumptions, the options and their trade-offs. Board members often ask for more scenarios or a further option, which sends the analysis back for another round.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: board settles on a preferred option

evidence.note: CalPERS held education days and strategy sessions over about a year before its vote; the pension client's study ran from 2020 to an April 2021 board decision. Workshop share and timing are author estimates.

steps.name: Client supplies latest valuation and cash flow update
steps.description: For the annual review the client's staff send the latest funded status, contribution and benefit cash flow forecast and any plan or policy changes since last year, usually from the actuary's latest valuation or roll-forward.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate; annual reviews reuse the latest valuation rather than a new projection.

steps.name: Refresh the annual policy tests
steps.description: The analyst updates the client's current mix, new capital market assumptions and valuation results in the model, re-runs expected return and risk for the approved mix, checks ranges, benchmarks and restrictions against how the portfolio was actually run during the year, and lists policy clauses that need updating.

error.defect_description: A stale input (old return assumption or benchmark) carries into the review.

evidence.note: Annual SIPP review and confirmation required; SIP&P sets out expected return from capital market assumptions. Hours are author estimates.

steps.name: Draft the recommendation and policy mark-up
steps.description: The portfolio strategist writes the recommendation paper (findings, recommended targets, ranges and benchmarks, expected return and risk, transition timetable for any change) and marks up the client's statement of investment policies and procedures, including how private asset under or overweights are remapped to public assets.
inputs: preferred option or annual review results

error.defect_description: Inconsistency between paper, tables and policy mark-up.

evidence.note: SIP&P content (targets, ranges, remapping of private assets, transition clauses) and IPS elements. Hours are author estimates.

steps.name: Head of portfolio construction reviews the advice
steps.description: The managing director checks the recommendation against the house view and other clients' advice for consistency, challenges the reasoning and tables, and returns it for changes where needed.

error.defect_description: An error passes review.

control.basis: The model manager internal review of client advice by the head of portfolio construction

evidence.note: Author estimate of review effort and 15% return rate.

steps.name: CIO approves the advice
steps.description: The chief investment officer reads the paper, confirms the recommended mix is one the model manager can implement within its pools, leverage and private market pacing, and signs off before anything goes to the client.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: The model manager delegation of authority: asset mix advice to client boards approved by the chief investment officer

evidence.note: Author estimate based on the CIO's role over portfolio construction in the organisation file.

steps.name: Review client materials and send the pre-read
steps.description: The director of client relationships checks the paper and presentation for the client's format and plain language, confirms the meeting agenda with the client's staff and sends the pre-read to staff and their investment consultant.

error.defect_description: Formatting or wording problem passes to the client.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Client staff and consultant review the draft
steps.description: The client's investment staff, and often its own investment consultant or actuary, review the draft and send comments or questions; significant comments send the paper back for revision before the committee meeting.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: The model manager collaborates with client boards, actuaries and external advisers; waits and revision share are author estimates.

steps.name: Present the recommendation to the client's investment committee
steps.description: The portfolio strategist and relationship manager present at the client's investment committee, answer questions and record the committee's decision to recommend the policy to the board, sometimes with amendments.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: The pension client's investment committee reviews and recommends the SIP&P to the board annually. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Client board approves the policy and asset mix
steps.description: The client's board approves or confirms the statement of investment policies and procedures and the strategic asset allocation at its next meeting, or asks for changes. Pension plan clients then file the amended policy with the pension regulator within 60 days.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Pension Benefits Act s. 22 and Regulation 909 s. 78: the administrator sets the SIPP, reviews and confirms or amends it at least annually and files amendments within 60 days; the insurance client board approves its SIPP each fiscal year

evidence.note: Annual review and approval by the client board and 60-day filing stated in the sources; branch shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Write the policy implementation memo
steps.description: The portfolio strategist turns the approved policy into implementation parameters: new targets and ranges by asset class and pool, policy benchmark weights, changed restrictions, the transition path from the old to the new mix and the date each change takes effect, and sends it to total portfolio management, risk, compliance and performance.

error.defect_description: A range or effective date in the memo differs from the approved policy.

evidence.note: The model manager must comply with the client SIP&P and SAA; new SAAs are phased in over years and transitions may sit outside ranges; memo content and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Update policy ranges and limits in the risk system
steps.description: A risk analyst loads the new policy weights, ranges and benchmark into the risk system so daily limit monitoring tests the client portfolio against the approved policy and its transition path.

error.defect_description: Range keyed wrongly, giving false or missed breach alerts.

evidence.note: Author estimate; daily monitoring against client policy ranges is described in the organisation file.

steps.name: Update the client's restrictions in the compliance engine
steps.description: A compliance analyst changes the coded rules for the client's account where the policy changed permitted investments, limits or leverage, tests them against current holdings and records the change.

error.defect_description: A rule change has the wrong scope.

control.basis: OSC decision of 17 May 2017, para 31(e): restrictions set out in each client's IMA and policy are built into controls that prevent contraventions

evidence.note: Control from the OSC decision; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Update the policy benchmark in the performance system
steps.description: A performance analyst sets the new policy benchmark weights and effective date for the client portfolio so returns are measured against the approved mix from the right month.

error.defect_description: Benchmark weight or start date wrong, restating later performance.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Load targets in the rebalancing model and cross-check all set-ups
steps.description: An analyst in total portfolio management loads the new targets, ranges and transition path into the rebalancing model, then compares the risk, compliance and performance set-ups line by line with the approved policy and memo; differences go back to the team that keyed them.

error.defect_description: A mismatch is missed and surfaces as a false breach or wrong benchmark.

control.basis: Independent check of policy parameters keyed by another team (maker-checker; common practice)

evidence.note: Author estimate; 10% mismatch rate assumed.

steps.name: Confirm the outcome to the client
steps.description: The relationship manager writes to the client confirming the approved policy, when each change takes effect and how the transition to any new mix will be reported, files the approved policy and board resolution, and closes the review in the CRM.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

exceptions.name: Board asks for more scenarios in a full study
exceptions.description: After an education workshop the board wants another option or stress case, sending the analysis back through modelling, risk review and a further workshop at a later meeting.

exceptions.name: Actuary data queries
exceptions.description: Projected cash flows do not tie to the valuation and go back to the actuary.

exceptions.name: Client staff or consultant revisions
exceptions.description: Comments from the client's staff or its own consultant require the paper to be reworked and re-approved internally before the committee.

exceptions.name: Board sends the policy back
exceptions.description: The board asks for changes, pushing approval to its next meeting, often a quarter later.

exceptions.name: Policy confirmed without change
exceptions.description: In a routine year the board confirms the existing policy and nothing needs to be re-keyed in systems.

exceptions.name: Client policy not finalised for over a year
exceptions.description: Governance disputes at the client stall approval, leaving assets in an interim mix, as with the judges' plan whose policy and SAA were still not final at March 2021.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from scoping to confirmed implementation
benchmarks.population: Annual policy reviews and periodic asset-liability studies for public pension and insurance clients

evidence.note: Derived, not measured: annual reviews are timed to one committee and one board meeting (author estimate about three to four months), while full studies took about a year (CalPERS November 2024 to November 2025; the pension client study started in 2020 and its SAA was approved in April 2021). With one full study in four reviews, p90 falls in the full-study range.
Cycle initiated November 2024; board vote November 2025.

benchmarks.population: The pension client (three to five years) and the insurance client (at least every four years)
Ontario pension plan administrators and the insurance client

evidence.note: SIPP reviewed and confirmed or amended at least annually.

benchmarks.population: The pension client SAA approved April 2021

evidence.note: The model manager to implement the new SAA over a four-year period.
Regulation 909 s. 78.

pain_points.description: Committee and board calendars set the pace: a comment or an extra scenario request moves approval to the next meeting, often a quarter later.

evidence.note: Full studies run over about a year of board sessions.

pain_points.description: The study waits on the client's actuary for liability projections that do not fit the actuary's own valuation cycle.

evidence.note: Author judgement from the dependency on client actuaries described by the model manager.

pain_points.description: Each client wants its own format and process, so similar analysis is rebuilt five times and cross-client consistency needs a separate review.

evidence.note: Organisation file notes each client keeps its own policy and report formats; consistency checking is an author judgement.

pain_points.description: Approved policy changes are re-keyed separately into risk, compliance, performance and rebalancing tools, so a cross-check is needed to catch mismatches.

evidence.note: Separate systems listed in the organisation file; re-keying risk is an author judgement.

pain_points.description: Disagreements inside a client's governance can stall approval for more than a year, leaving assets in an interim mix that the asset manager cannot change on its own.

evidence.note: The judges' plan SIP&P and SAA were not finalised by 31 March 2021 as expected because of discussions among the board, the sponsor and the judges' association.

sources.title: The pension client 2021 Annual Report

sources.title: Insurance fund: statement of investment policies and procedures (The insurance client web page)
sources.supports: The insurance client board approves the SIPP and reviews it at least once each fiscal year; detailed asset-liability study of the policy mix no less often than every four years; the model manager sole investment manager; derivatives may be used for rebalancing; liquidity coverage monitored at least monthly; performance, risk and compliance reviewed at least quarterly; policy asset mix with minimum, target and maximum by asset class; private over or underweights remapped to public assets and the model manager outlines a plan to reach targets when outside ranges; non-traded investments valued at least annually and reviewed quarterly, public investments at least monthly

sources.title: Our Approach (The model manager web page)

sources.title: The model manager (The pension client investments page)
sources.supports: The model manager invests under an investment management agreement and must comply with the pension client's SIP&P including the SAA; regular performance and risk reporting; cost recovery only

sources.title: The model manager, Commission and Director decisions (exemptions for the model manager and its investment pools)

assumptions: One review in four is a full asset-liability study, from three to five year study cycles across five portfolios; the rest are annual reviews.

The routing at s01 sends full studies through s02 to s08 and annual reviews through s09 and s10; both join at s11. The simulator draws branches independently, so loop counts are averages, not per-path rules.
External steps (actuary, client staff, committee and board) carry zero touch time; client effort is inside the waits.
Hands-on hours for a full study (about 250 to 400 hours including workshop rounds) and an annual review (about 60 to 100 hours) are author estimates; the asset manager publishes no effort data.
The cycle time benchmark is derived from two dated full studies (CalPERS, the pension client) and the annual review requirement; there is no published distribution.
risk_analyst, compliance_analyst, performance_analyst and tpm_analyst are organisation file roles not listed on this process_map entry; they are added for the system updates after approval.
The pension regulator filing within 60 days is done by the client and is not on the asset manager's path, so it is described in s17 rather than modelled as a wait.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's ranges (Job Bank wages, 1.35 loading).
